title: Close the gaps in the record-session pin's read regex, or name them out of scope
evidence: Done by PR {PR}: packages/health-core/src/record-session-erase.pins.test.ts now finds @internal reads in the TypeScript syntax tree instead of a regex. It catches reads through casts and parentheses, typed, parameter, for-of, nested and defaulted destructuring, and a member chain split across lines; each was a failing case under the old regex. It leaves names in comments and strings alone, and cloudUnreachable joins the session-only names, so a caller's own open() options pass. The test comment lists the forms still out of scope (no type checker). Was: From the review of PR 1702 (A24): the READ regex in packages/health-core/src/record-session-erase.pins.test.ts:36-38 still misses some reads of RecordSession's @internal names, all missed by the old regex too: a read through a cast or parentheses, such as `(session as unknown as Inside).dispatch(...)`, the repo's own way in (record-session.session.test.ts:1287); typed destructuring (`const { saveMode }: RecordSession = s`), and parameter or for-of destructuring; nested or defaulted destructuring; a member chain split across lines. One false-red risk: `cloudUnreachable` is both an @internal field and a public open() option, so `const { cloudUnreachable } = opts` in a caller would fail the pin; nothing does that today. Remedy: add the typed form and a cast form, plus a negative case for cloudUnreachable from opts; for the rest, say in the test comment which forms are out of scope. (H99)
